title: phase_0
text: Linear growth adds the same amount each step. Exponential growth multiplies by the same factor. Starting with two and multiplying by one and a half gives two, three, four and a half, and six and three quarters.

title: phase_1
text: In a times b to the t, a is the initial value at time zero and b is the per-step factor. A factor of one point five means a fifty percent increase, not a one point five percent increase.

title: phase_2
text: A factor between zero and one gives decay. Multiplying by one half repeatedly halves the amount. Zero exponent gives one, so the initial value remains a; negative exponents reverse the multiplication.

title: phase_3
text: For a rate r expressed as a decimal, growth uses one plus r and decay uses one minus r. Check the time unit: a monthly rate and a yearly exponent do not belong in the same model without conversion.
